title: A Glacier in Antarctica Bleeds Red Water

scenes.text: A glacier in Antarctica bleeds red water.
It's called Blood Falls, and it pours out of Taylor Glacier.
The water is so salty it stays liquid in Antarctic cold.
It's rich in iron. When it hits the air, the iron rusts and turns the water red.
Scientists think the brine was trapped under the ice for more than a million years.
Radar traced it almost 1,000 feet into the glacier, through a hidden network of brine pools.
A waterfall of rust, from a million years ago.

description:
A glacier in Antarctica bleeds red water.
Blood Falls gets its color from iron-rich salty brine that was trapped under Taylor Glacier for more than a million years.
What would you name it? Comment below.
